source.title: A Bayesian Model Selection Criterion for Selecting Pretraining Checkpoints

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies pretraining checkpoint selection and downstream transfer accuracy. Its results do not test same-distribution generalization gaps or any listed version.
record.gate_note: The study reports associations between pretraining metrics and downstream transfer accuracy, not training-versus-test error on natural labels. Those transfer findings are recorded as results outside the listed versions. Cited findings about implicit bias and generalization are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study tests checkpoint metrics as predictors of downstream transfer accuracy, not any listed claim version. Its batch-size sweeps hold optimizer steps fixed, not epochs as V5 requires. Its free-energy metric is neither V7's magnitude-aware sharpness nor evaluated against the train–test generalization gap.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose downstream free energy as an adaptability criterion and empirically support pretraining WBIC as a practical proxy across the tested datasets and architectures. The predictive-performance guarantee applies to Bayesian adaptation; a direct guarantee for their ordinary fine-tuning procedure remains unestablished.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures pretraining free energy and transfer performance; it does not test the original studies' interventions or same-distribution generalization-gap measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports downstream transfer results across learning-rate, batch-size, and momentum sweeps; it also evaluates full and few-shot fine-tuning settings and reports differing correlations by pretraining metric and evaluation setting.

fits_no_version.finding: WBIC-estimated pretraining free energy has the strongest absolute Pearson correlation with transfer accuracy among the three metrics in Table 1: −0.820 for full fine-tuning and −0.8901 for few-shot fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower pretraining free energy predicts better downstream adaptation more strongly than geometric complexity or neural collapse in the tested CIFAR-FS ResNet-18 checkpoint sample.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 2 and 3 report better downstream transfer from checkpoints pretrained with smaller batches, larger learning rates, or higher momentum. Batch sweeps use 50,000 optimizer steps for every batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under fixed pretraining step budgets, these hyperparameter changes correlate with lower pretraining WBIC and better full and few-shot adaptation on CIFAR-FS/ResNet-18 and mini-ImageNet/VGG-16.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267, 2025
record.problems: The central reported WBIC-to-transfer trends in Figures 2 and 3 are qualitative in the supplied text. Table 1 reports correlations from one CIFAR-FS ResNet-18 checkpoint analysis; the paper notes that the direct theoretical link to predictive performance is established only for Bayesian adaptation.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 and Figure 3 report qualitative WBIC-versus-transfer trends for learning-rate, batch-size, and momentum sweeps on CIFAR-FS/ResNet-18 and mini-ImageNet/VGG-16, including full and few-shot evaluation. They are not represented as additional rows because the supplied text gives no separate numeric values for those figure results; the paper's qualitative description is captured in the excerpt.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the contrasting held-out performance on random and natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and remedies for its penalty; the reported pretraining sweeps instead fix optimizer steps and evaluate downstream adaptation.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of train–test gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The qualitative figure results are already declared in rows_left_out. Excerpt E1 substitutes pretraining free energy for the downstream free energy described in its supporting passage; the pretraining proxy requires the paper's additional assumptions.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and same-distribution generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and their generalization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and held-out generalization.
Batch-size effects on train-test generalization gaps.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
